phases.name: On-Ramp
phases.goal: Build the habit. Three easy runs and two lifts a week until it's automatic. Long run to 5 miles. Easy pace feels natural.

phases.name: The Course
phases.goal: Six months. Build the runner and the body: half-marathon fitness with hills, a real hypertrophy program, four tune-up races, then Glacier.

phases.name: The Marathon
phases.goal: Recover, rebuild in the summer heat, then the marathon-specific build: 16, 18, 20, taper, Monumental.

sessions.title: GLACIER HALF MARATHON
sessions.subtitle: RACE
details: 6:00 AM MDT start near Kiowa. First FIVE miles uphill: run them at easy effort, no matter how slow the watch says. Everyone who goes out hard here walks at mile 9.
Top of the climb → downhill past Two Medicine Lake → finish on the lawn of Glacier Park Lodge. Let the downhill carry you; short quick steps.
Fuel: gel at 40 min and every 35 after. Water every aid station (there are five). Four-hour cutoff is not a concern.
Goal: finish, look up, enjoy it. This is the race you planned a whole trip around.

sessions.title: INDIANAPOLIS MONUMENTAL MARATHON — 26.2
sessions.subtitle: RACE
details: 8:00 AM, Indiana State House. Flat. Cool. Your family on the course.
Miles 1–20: marathon pace, and if anything, 10–15 seconds slower. The crowd and the adrenaline will beg you to go faster. Every first-timer who listens pays for it at mile 22.
Fuel: gel at 40 min, then every 35. Water every station; sports drink from mile 10. You practiced all of this.
Mile 20 is where the race starts. Break the last 10K into five one-mile wins. Whatever you have at 24, spend it.
Goal: cross the line. A year ago your longest run was a 5K.
